messages:

Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff — quick inputs on model needs

Hi Ben / Grace / Jordan,

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. I promised to share a concise profile so you could recommend an initial model shortlist and ballpark token budget. Attached: Pillar_token_profile.xlsx (contains hourly traffic sketch, example prompts, and a sample of conversational history lengths). Quick highlights:

- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for intake nurses (short free-text -> structured summary + suggested disposition).
- Expected steady-state: ~6M tokens/month in month 1, with conservative growth to 12M by month 3.
- Peak hour: ~1,800 requests/hour during morning surge (08:00–10:00 PT), average request ~220 tokens in/out.
- Context needs: typically prior 3 messages + patient notes (often 400–800 tokens). A small subset (~5%) needs expanded context up to ~2,400 tokens for multi-note cases.
- Latency target: 300–450ms p50 generation for short prompts; p95 under 1.5s is acceptable if we use fallback.

We want a shortlist that balances cost and accuracy — pragmatic picks for Phase 1 (pilot, 4–6 week). Also flag any configuration (context pinning, prefix caching) that materially reduces cost.

Legal may loop if you recommend private deployment / on-prem. I cc'd them for visibility.

Thanks,
Anita
Anita Gomez
Head of Product Operations, Pillar Health

Hi Anita — thanks for the profile, that’s super helpful. I ran a quick pass with Grace and Jordan and attached a short PDF with an initial shortlist and high-level reasoning (redwood_model_shortlist_v1.pdf). Key recommendations up-front:

- Pilot shortlist (Phase 1):
  1) small/highly-optimized LM (e.g., 7B quantized variant) for the majority of requests — low-cost, sub-200ms p50 on Dedicated; good for structured-output templates.
  2) medium context LM (e.g., 16B quantized long-context) for 5–10% of requests that need 1,200–2,400 token windows.
  3) fallback LLM (higher quality, 70B-class) for complex edge-cases and escalation responses (log/queue for human review).

- Cost ballpark (very preliminary): assuming your Month 1 mix (6M tokens) and the above split, we estimate ~USD 6k–9k/month on Redwood Dedicated standard configs. Peak hour provisioning: reserve capacity for ~2k rps bursts with autoscale buffer. I attached token_estimates.csv which shows three scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic).

Next steps: can we set a 45-minute technical workshop Thursday (10/16) to align on context pinning strategies and to validate the 5% long-context fraction? Grace — would you be able to lead the session and bring the context caching/latency tradeoff options? Jordan — please include a preliminary Dedicated capacity sketch.

Anita — if this looks reasonable I’ll add Legal’s ask on Private deployment feasibility into the same call so we can triage.

Best,
Ben

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff — quick inputs on model needs

Ben / Jordan — quick internal notes before the Thursday workshop. Quoting Anita’s traffic so we have context:

> - Peak hour: ~1,800 requests/hour, avg request ~220 tokens in/out
> - Context: typical 400–800 tokens; 5% up to ~2,400 tokens

Operational implications:
- Batching vs latency: continuous batching will help cost but will add 30–80ms p50 depending on config; still within your SLA. For the 5% long-context, we should route to dedicated long-context workers to avoid KV cache pollution.
- Prefix pinning: we can aggressively pin templated patient-history prefixes (top 80% of tokens) to reduce generation work — expect 10–18% token cost savings on average.
- Quantization: recommend starting with 4-bit quantization for the 7B/16B picks to hit the latency/cost targets; keep a non-quantized higher-capacity model for the fallback.
- Capacity sketch: pilot (6M tokens/mo) ~= sustained 8 QPS avg with 2k hourly peak. For Dedicated sizing, assume baseline pool of 4x A10-equivalent GPUs with autoscale to 8 for peak windows. Jordan — can you draft a short GCE/AWS instance mix?

I’ll prepare a 1-slide tradeoff that shows expected p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens for each model.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff — quick inputs on model needs

All — draft capacity note before I put a slide in the call. Using Grace’s baseline: pilot = 6M tokens/mo, peak ~1,800 req/hr (2k burst). Assumptions: avg token per request 220, average generation tokens 120 (we separate in/out).

Estimate (very rough):
- Baseline pool: 4 x A10-equivalent (or 2 x A100-80GB) for the small/medium models (quantized). That supports the 2k peak with p50 ~250–350ms for short windows.
- Long-context workers: 1 x A100-80GB (or 2 x A10 with sequence-sliced config) dedicated to 5% long requests; autoscale to 2 for sustained higher peaks.
- Fallback routing: send >1,200 token context or flagged low-confidence outputs to 70B-class fallback hosted in a separate pool (on-demand).

Provisional risk: if Pillar increases long-context fraction >10% we'll need to move more of their traffic to long-context workers which raises monthly cost by ~40%.

I’ll join Thurs and present these numbers; if Legal pushes Private deployment we should prep a quick delta-cost estimate for an on-prem package.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

   - Primary: 7B quantized variant (fast, low cost) — route 85% traffic.
   - Secondary: 16B long-context quantized variant — route 10% traffic for 1,200–2,400 token windows.
   - Fallback: 70B-class (non-quantized) — route ~5% for escalations and human-in-the-loop reviews.

2) Token budget estimate (Month 1):

   - Upside: 12M tokens/mo (by month 3).

3) Operational suggestions:

   - Route >1,200 token contexts to long-context pool; set automatic fallback threshold on token-confidence score.
   - Instrument early: add token-level cost tags and p95 latency alerts to the onboarding dashboard (we’ll share a dashboard link post-call).

4) Next steps: confirm the workshop time and whether Legal wants a short Private deployment delta-cost note. Also please confirm the 5% long-context fraction — if it’s actually closer to 10% we’ll update capacity slides.

Thanks — we’ll come ready with a short benchmarking table and a Dedicated sizing sketch.
